title: Auditflow: evidence bundle guidance for customer questionnaires
content:
Purpose:
This note is a compact operational guide for packaging a reproducible evidence bundle we can hand to customers during security questionnaires and audits. It focuses on RBAC v2 mappings, audit log schema highlights, and a lightweight SIEM export/automation pattern so we can produce a verifiable package quickly without manual digging.

Audience:
- Solutions engineers responding to questionnaires
- Security engineers producing audit artifacts
- Customer success teams preparing evidence handoffs

Scope and non-goals:
- Scope: artifacts derived from RBAC v2, audit logs for authentication/authorization, SIEM-ready CSV/NDJSON exports, and an automated bundle that ties logs -> evidence mapping.
- Non-goal: full legal attestations or penetration test reports. This is an engineering + operational handoff playbook.

Quick summary of the recommended bundle contents (single ZIP delivered to customer):
1) index.md (human-readable manifest) — explains what is included, time range, and hashes
2) rbac-v2-export.jsonl — exported RBAC v2 role, policy, and membership snapshots (timestamped)
3) audit-logs-YYYYMMDD.ndjson (one or more files) — authentication + authorization events, schema version label
4) siem-mapping.csv — column mapping between our internal fields and common SIEM ingestion fields (Splunk/Elastic/QRadar)
5) evidence-mapping.csv — the questionnaire questions (short id) mapped to specific files and line numbers or event ids in the logs
6) redwood-configs/ — sanitized config snippets (small) showing retention, KMS identifier, and log-export pipeline definition
7) verification.md — instructions for how the customer can verify hashes and reproduce queries against raw logs

RBAC v2 snapshot guidance:
- Export timing: snapshot at audit time + preceding 30 days for context. Include record of who changed policies (actor id) and change timestamp.
- Minimum fields to include per role/policy: id, name, description, version/etag, granted-actions (canonical list), resource-scope, created_by, created_at, last_modified_by, last_modified_at.
- Membership: map principal (user/service-account) -> assigned-roles (include assignment id and assignment timestamp).
- Sanitization rules: redact ephemeral secrets, replace UUIDs for internal-only services with stable surrogates (prefix mapping included in index.md).

Audit log schema (baseline v1.2 we publish internally):
- Top-level fields we always provide:
  - event_id (UUID)
  - timestamp (ISO8601 UTC)
  - event_type (authn, authz, role_change, config_change, keystore_op, api_call)
  - actor_id (subject performing action)
  - actor_type (user | service_account | system)
  - target_id (resource acted on)
  - target_type (model | endpoint | infra | policy)
  - action (canonical action string, e.g., token:create, role:assign, inference:invoke)
  - outcome (success | failure | denied)
  - request_id (correlates to API request)
  - extra (free-form JSON blob with context: ip, region, model_version, route)
- Minimal audit event size: keep extra small; surface fields expected by customer auditors (actor id, what changed, before/after when applicable).
- Provenance: each log file must include file-level metadata header (schema_version, exported_at, earliest_ts, latest_ts, exported_by).

SIEM export considerations (practical patterns):
- Deliver exports as NDJSON for Elastic/Sumo/Splunk; provide CSV alternative for manual review.
- Timestamp normalization: all timestamps in UTC with sub-second precision.
- Field name mappings (deliver siem-mapping.csv with columns: redwood_field, common_field, notes). Example mappings included in the bundle: event_id -> event_id, timestamp -> @timestamp, actor_id -> user.name, action -> action.name, outcome -> outcome.status, request_id -> trace.id.
- Performance: when we expect very large log sets, deliver a sampled slice (e.g., full logs for the audit window + a 24h full segment) and indicate sampling logic in index.md.

Automated evidence-bundle workflow (recommended scriptable flow):
1) Inputs: customer questionnaire id + requested time range + requester contact + retention/PII constraints.
2) Pre-check: ensure requested time range is within retention; if not, return template with retention policy and recommended alternate windows.
3) RBAC snapshot export: call internal /admin/rbac/export?at=<ts>. Store file with etag and signer metadata.
4) Log export: run log-export job by filter (service=redwood-inference AND time-range). Include request_id and role_change events.
5) Sanitize: run sanitizer to scrub PII/keys according to policy config (record which scrub rules applied).
6) Produce siem-mapping.csv and evidence-mapping.csv by cross-referencing question -> required artifact.
7) Sign bundle and compute SHA256 of each file. Produce verification.md.
8) Upload to customer-approved S3/GDrive folder and notify SRE and SE for handoff.

Checklist for solutions engineers before sending to customer:
- [ ] Confirm time window and retention with customer success
- [ ] Verify RBAC export includes policy change history for the window
- [ ] Confirm sanitizer rules applied and list of scrubbed fields
- [ ] Attach SIEM mapping file and a short example ingestion query (Elastic DSL and Splunk SPL)
- [ ] Add contact for follow-up (security eng on-call)

Common Customer Questionnaire Q&A patterns (editable snippets):
Q: Provide a list of roles and role descriptions in scope.
A: See rbac-v2-export.jsonl (role records) and membership snapshot in the bundle; we also include a human-readable summary in index.md.

Q: How long are audit logs retained?
A: Default: 90 days hot, 365 days cold (compressed) for hosted API customers. For Dedicated/Private customers, retention is configurable; the bundle will state configured retention and provide exported artifacts for the requested window.

Q: How do you demonstrate separation of duties?
A: We map role assignments and change events; the RBAC snapshot + config_change events in audit logs provide evidence of who approved/created role assignments. We include request_id linking UI/API action to actor.

Open implementation notes & caveats:
- We cannot include raw user plaintext PII (email addresses) unless customer has a DPA-approved need; prefer pseudonymization with stable mapping.
- For very large customers, prefer an interactive review session rather than handing millions of lines of log data.
- Some historical data may be in legacy schema; include a schema translation note and sample translator script if needed.

Examples / small snippets to include in index.md:
- "Export window: 2026-01-15T00:00:00Z -> 2026-01-22T23:59:59Z"
- "Signer: audite-bot@redwood.ai (key id: key-7b3a)"
- "Sanitization: emails pseudonymized with stable SHA256 mapping (mapping file: sanitized/mapping-users.csv)"

Verification steps for customer (short):
1) Download bundle and confirm checksums against verification.md
2) Use the sample Elastic DSL query in siem-examples/ to run on your SIEM or run the included grep/sed examples against NDJSON to validate event id linkage
3) Contact security@redwood.ai with request_id if any mismatch is found

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Add small script templates (Python) for export -> sanitize -> sign (PR tracker: github.com/redwood/inference/PR-973).
- Align field names with upcoming internal schema v1.3 (TBD: replace "actor_type" with "subject_type").
- Run tabletop with SEs to validate index.md clarity (owner: Marcus).

References and helpful links:
- Internal: Confluence Auditflow overview (linked in metadata)
- Example PR with exporter code: github.com/redwood/inference/PR-973

End of draft.
